name: Japan-US Strategic Investment Initiative (MOU of 4 Sep 2025)
notes: US investment committee proposes projects and Japan funds them through per-project SPVs with JBIC loans and NEXI insurance; two batches (US$36bn Feb 2026, US$73bn Mar 2026) are gas power, crude export, synthetic diamonds and GE Vernova Hitachi SMRs. No published sector strategy, KPIs or reciprocal commitments; selection is US-led (E42).

name: US-Japan critical minerals and rare earths framework (Oct 2025) with the Supply Security Rapid Response Group
notes: Commits financing for selected projects within six months, a ministerial within 180 days, pricing measures for non-China supply, scrap recycling and a complementary stockpile arrangement; non-binding and names no amounts or projects. Whether the Rapid Response Group has met is unverified.

name: US-Japan Action Plan on Critical Minerals (19 Mar 2026)
notes: Strategic trade policies and border mechanisms to protect downstream industries; foundation for a binding plurilateral agreement supported by price floors.

name: US-Japan Critical Minerals Agreement (28 Mar 2023)
notes: Covers cobalt, graphite, lithium, manganese and nickel; its main function (FTA status for the 30D credit) is largely moot after the credit ended for vehicles acquired after 30 Sep 2025.

name: US-Japan trade agreements (USJTA and DTA 2019; July 2025 deal and EO 14345)
notes: Goods and digital agreements of 2019 plus the 2025 tariff deal; the IEEPA reciprocal rate fell with the Feb 2026 Supreme Court ruling and the reported replacement is a 12.5% Section 301 tariff; Section 232 duties continue.

name: US-Japan Economic Policy Consultative Committee (Economic 2+2)
notes: Ministerial economic-security dialogue launched 2022; agreed in 2024 to meet periodically; no 2026 meeting found.

name: DFC-JBIC cooperation memorandum
notes: Renewal reported (critical minerals and energy transition in the Indo-Pacific); date and any joint deals not captured.

name: Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework (May 2026)
notes: Up to US$20bn to be mobilised for secure critical-mineral supply chains (secondary source).

name: US-EU framework trade arrangement and its 2026 legal basis (EU-level, applies to Germany)
notes: 15% all-in US tariff for EU goods against EU tariff cuts, with non-binding energy and investment pledges; the US legal basis moved from IEEPA to Section 122 to Section 301 in 2026 and EU-specific caps under 301 are unconfirmed. The EU regulation has suspension and sunset clauses.

name: EU countermeasures and Section 232 friction (EU-level, applies to Germany)
notes: EUR 93bn of EU countermeasures stay suspended with no end date while US 50% steel, aluminium and copper tariffs and derivative coverage remain contested.

name: US-EU critical minerals MOU and action plan (EU-level, applies to Germany)
notes: Non-binding April 2026 MOU on diversification and export-control coordination; price floors and a plurilateral club are only to be explored; no German-US project list or money.

name: G7 Critical Minerals Action Plan and Minerals Security Partnership
notes: Both countries sit in the G7 plan and the MSP Forum; projects and financing run through members, with no German-US bilateral pipeline.

name: US-Germany Climate and Energy Partnership (2022) and TTC
notes: Earlier dialogue formats (2022 energy partnership, TTC) with no confirmed current activity; superseded in practice by EU-level 2025-26 arrangements.

name: Korea-Japan Supply Chain Partnership Arrangement and Industrial and Trade Policy Dialogue
notes: Mar 2026 ministerial arrangement: early warning, emergency meeting within five days and prior consultation before harmful measures, reviewed at a standing dialogue. No project list, funding or KPIs published; implementation meeting in Sept 2026 is unverified.

name: Korea-Japan Mineral Resources Cooperation Dialogue
notes: Two rounds (Feb and Dec 2025) agreed to support joint third-country development and coordinate in MSP and IEA. No named projects and no JOGMEC-KOMIR agreement found; Korea's state agency only began to regain overseas investment powers in 2026.

name: Japan-ROK Hydrogen and Ammonia Cooperation Dialogue and company links
notes: Government dialogue since 2024 plus company MoUs (JERA with Samsung C&T and Lotte Fine Chemical; KNOC-JOGMEC). Projects are exploratory with no amounts; certification and standards work proposed by business federations.

name: RCEP and Korea's CPTPP accession question
notes: RCEP is the only agreement covering both; there is no bilateral FTA. Japan and business groups support Korea's CPTPP entry but Korea has not applied and the president said entry is unlikely in his term.

name: 2019 export-control dispute and its 2023 settlement
notes: Japan's curbs on three semiconductor materials and the white-list removals were reversed in 2023 with Korea's WTO withdrawal; the episode defines Korean sensitivity to Japanese materials dependence and a consultation clause now sits in the SCPA.

name: US-Japan-ROK trilateral supply-chain early warning and critical-minerals dialogue
notes: Camp David (2023) pilot early-warning system, with a Sept 2025 senior-officials commitment to deepen critical-minerals dialogue. No published pipeline or finance; no 2026 trilateral economic-security dialogue statement was found.

name: FKI-Keidanren business conferences
notes: Annual business conferences (32nd Tokyo 2025, 33rd Seoul Oct 2026) issue joint statements on supply chains, hydrogen standards and stockpiling; non-binding and with no projects.

name: Australia-US Free Trade Agreement
notes: Goods and services FTA with a Joint Committee; it did not shield Australia from the Section 122 or Section 301 tariffs and does not address critical-minerals finance.

name: US-Australia Critical Minerals and Rare Earths Framework (Oct 2025)
notes: US$1bn each toward a US$8.5bn pipeline, delivered through EFA, EXIM, DoW and OSC for named projects (Alcoa gallium, Arafura, Lynas, Tronox, Sunrise); EXIM letters are non-binding and no joint price floor exists beyond the DoW-Lynas NdPr floor.

name: Climate, Critical Minerals and Clean Energy Transformation Compact (2023)
notes: Established a Clean Energy Industrial Transformation forum and a ministerial critical-minerals taskforce with no amounts; largely superseded in practice by the 2025 framework.

name: Quad Critical Minerals Initiative
notes: Quad aim to mobilise US$20bn for mining, processing and recycling; no project list or published delivery mechanism.

name: Australian offtake and stockpile tools aligned with US reserves (Strategic Reserve, Production Tax Incentive)
notes: Australia's A$1.2bn reserve and 10% processing offset from July 2027 sit alongside the US Project Vault and DoW price floors; interoperability, joint price floor and uranium coverage are not set.

name: US tariff arrangement on Australia (Section 122 then Section 301, Section 232)
notes: Australia moved from 10% (Section 122) to 12.5% (Section 301 forced-labor band) in July 2026; Section 232 metals tariffs continue; a forced-labour import ban might lower the band.

name: KORUS Free Trade Agreement
notes: Tariff-preference FTA with consultative mechanisms, amended in 2018; it no longer sets the effective US tariff on most Korean goods and does not cover Section 232 or investment-fund terms.

name: US-Korea Strategic Investment MOU and Special Act (US$350bn)
notes: Korea funds US-approved projects (US$200bn strategic plus US$150bn shipbuilding) up to US$20bn a year through the Korea-US Strategic Investment Corporation; three projects named in Oct 2026 but MASGA financing and project-level terms are unsettled and selection is US-led.

name: US tariff arrangement and its legal basis (15% deal, IEEPA ruling, Section 122/301/232)
notes: The 15% country tariff lost its IEEPA basis on 20 Feb 2026 and was replaced by Section 122 then a 12.5% Section 301 tariff; Section 232 caps (autos 15%, chips MFN, polysilicon 15%) remain; Korea seeks assurance against excess-capacity tariffs above 15%.

name: US-Korea civil nuclear cooperation (123 revision, Westinghouse-KHNP, reactor build-out)
notes: Talks on 123 Agreement revision and enrichment are ongoing; Westinghouse settlement of Jan 2025 is in force; Korean stake in Westinghouse and eight-reactor US programme are under commercial negotiation with no published project list.

name: Government-backed Korean plants in US supply chains (Korea Zinc Crucible smelter, Qcells, battery and grid plants)
notes: Mostly company-led plants; the only direct US government equity is the Department of War stake in the Korea Zinc smelter JV; no bilateral critical-minerals list or offtake exists.

name: Minerals Security Partnership and FORGE
notes: Multilateral co-financing forum Korea chaired until June 2026; no named project pipeline or bilateral US-Korea commitments.

name: KAFTA and RCEP
notes: Tariff-free goods trade since 2014 with phase-outs complete by 2023; no dispute found; rules of origin for critical-minerals inputs not assessed.

name: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and Critical Minerals Working Group
notes: Working group, A$50m initial Australian pot and leader-level contact since 2021; no published project list or KPIs, and no 2025-26 joint statement was found.

name: EFA-KEXIM co-financing channel for critical minerals
notes: 2023 MoU enables co-financing; the visible uses are KEXIM's US$150m LOI for Arafura and Korean-bank debt for the POSCO-Pilbara plant; no pipeline of projects is published.

name: Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement (2015)
notes: Tariff elimination plus investment and procurement chapters; Korea's complaint over Canada's 75% FTA-partner steel quota is unresolved and the 2026 energy meeting leans on CKFTA crude preferences.

name: Critical-minerals and energy-security MOU (2023) and 2026 stockpiling track
notes: Non-binding MOU with an action plan; the June 2026 meeting set a joint stockpiling plan due end-2026 but no volumes, projects or funds are published.

name: Industrial cooperation MOU and Canada-Korea Industrial Cooperation Committee (Jan 2026)
notes: Committee and mobility forum target a Korean auto and battery footprint in Canada; Korean battery projects exist (Windsor, Becancour) but the MOU has no published pipeline, finance line or KPIs.

name: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, Security and Defence Partnership and 2+2 dialogues
notes: Leader and ministerial channel with a biennial 2+2 and an Action Plan being updated; the defence-industrial link weakened when Canada chose TKMS in Jul 2026, with Hanwha kept only as a fallback.
